suggestions.title: Strike Friday's ham curl set — your own note says you skipped it

rationale.science: When progress or a lift looks off, check measurement and adherence before anything else (Alhassan 2008) — and on a cut, load is the signal that protects lean tissue, so a load built on a set that never happened is worse than no progression at all (Schoenfeld 2017; Grgic 2021).
rationale.data: Friday's session note reads 'Ham curl skipped this sesh for time. Abnormal.' The log for the same session shows 120 x 12,12. Every other lift on Friday carries an effort score — calves 2, extension 0, hack 0, abs 0, hanging 0 — and the ham curl is the only one with none at all, on a lift you scored at 2 in the tank on both 7/24 and 7/28. This is the second time: on 7/23 your note said you skipped the pronated curl for time while the log showed 40 x 12,12, and you ruled the note right.
rationale.relationship: The app has already acted on the phantom set — it wrote 'HAM CURL: 12,12 tops the window, 1 rep up on last time. Repeat it and the load queues itself.' So a single real session from here queues you a load increase off a baseline you never actually set, which is precisely the unearned bump that cratered your extension to 9,6 back on 7/21.

suggestions.predict: Strike it and ham curl stays at 120 until you genuinely put up 12,12 twice — the right answer. Leave it and your next leg day queues 125 off one real session plus one phantom one, and 125 opens light and gets reverted.

suggestions.title: Extension 155 is open and earned — run it, and 9,8 is a win

apply.to: Leg extension 155 — debut next lower day; open at ~1 RIR, target 9,8

rationale.science: On a deficit you defend load and advance it where it is actually earned rather than chasing volume — load is what holds lean tissue while calories are low (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021), and one to three reps in reserve is enough stimulus without buying recovery cost you can't pay.
rationale.data: 150 has gone 6,9 (7/24) then 8,7 (7/28) then 10,9 on Friday, and the app re-owned it: 'EXTENSION 150 RE-OWNED — 9,9 — the 155 gate reopens, earned.' The last time you were at 155 was 7/21, where you had self-bumped there without owning 9,9 first; it cratered to 9,6 and reverted.
rationale.relationship: 155 is 3.3% more load than 150, and on your app's own reps-per-load slope that is worth about 1.3 reps — so from 10,9 the honest landing zone is 9,8, not another 10,9. The difference from July is that this time the gate opened because you earned it rather than because you reached for it. Watch set two: that is where 155 fell over last time (9 then 6), and the opener was never the problem.

suggestions.predict: Debut lands 9,8 or better. Anything at or above 8,8 is a clean debut and 155 holds. If it comes in under that, read it as an opener taken too cautiously rather than the load being too heavy — that is the exact fix that just moved 150 from 8,7 to 10,9.
